facts.statement: Kiangyousteus is an extinct genus containing only one species, the Kiangyousteus yohii.
facts.quote: Kiangyousteus is an extinct monotypic genus of dunkleosteid

facts.statement: Fossils of Kiangyousteus were found in the Guanwu Formation in Sichuan province, south-western China.
facts.quote: Kiangyousteus is an extinct monotypic genus of dunkleosteid from the Middle Devonian: Givetian aged Guanwu Formation in the Sichuan province of south-western China

facts.statement: Professor S. H. Yoh of Peking University discovered the fossils in 1953 in the Jiangyou district of Sichuan Province.
facts.quote: Kiangyousteus is named after Jiangyou (formerly 'Kiangyou') district of Sichuan Province, the location where the fossils were found in 1953 by Professor S. H. Yoh of Peking University

facts.statement: The genus name Kiangyousteus honors the Jiangyou district where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: Kiangyousteus is named after Jiangyou (formerly 'Kiangyou') district of Sichuan Province

facts.statement: The genus Kiangyousteus was described by Liu in 1955.
Kiangyousteus lived during the Middle Devonian, specifically the Givetian stage.
Kiangyousteus lived between 387.95 and 382.31 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Givetian to Givetian (387.95 to 382.31 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kiangyousteus is classified as a dunkleosteid.
facts.quote: Kiangyousteus is an extinct monotypic genus of dunkleosteid

facts.statement: Kiangyousteus belongs to the family Dunkleosteidae.
facts.quote: Kiangyousteus belongs to the family Dunkleosteidae

facts.statement: The parent group of Kiangyousteus is Pachyosteomorphi.
Kiangyousteus is classified in the class Placodermi.
A 2016 study suggests that the status of Dunkleosteidae as a clade separate from Dunkleosteoidea is in doubt.
facts.quote: Alternatively, the subsequent 2016 Zhu et al. study using a larger morphological dataset recovered Panxiosteidae well outside of Dunkleosteoidea, leaving the status of Dunkleosteidae as a clade grouping separate from Dunkleosteoidea in doubt

rejected.statement: The type species Kiangyousteus yohii was the first known arthrodire discovered in Asia.
rejected.quote: The type species, Kiangyousteus yohii, was the first known arthrodire from Asia
